## Discover the pipeline after preprocessing

A pipeline records the preprocessing steps applied to an experiment. Start by
normalizing and imputing the bundled glycoproteomics experiment with ordinary
function calls:

```{r}
library(glyclean)

original <- glyexp::as_glycoproteomic_se(glyexp::real_experiment)
cleaned <- normalize_total_area(original)
cleaned <- impute_min_prob(cleaned, q = 0.01, seed = 42)
```

These calls automatically add a pipeline to the experiment's metadata. Use
`get_pipeline()` to retrieve it and print the recorded steps:

```{r}
history <- get_pipeline(cleaned)
history

identical(history, S4Vectors::metadata(cleaned)$pipeline)
```

A `glyclean_pipeline` is a list of steps. Each step contains a `function` and its
`parameters`, in the order they were applied. The printed summary shows the
function names and their parameters.

Automatic functions record the actual functions chosen. For example,
`auto_normalize()` selects median normalization for this glycoproteomics
experiment, so its history contains `normalize_median()`:

```{r}
automatically_normalized <- auto_normalize(original)
get_pipeline(automatically_normalized)
```

## Reproduce preprocessing from its history

Apply the recorded history to the same original experiment to reproduce the
preprocessing exactly:

```{r}
replayed <- apply_pipeline(original, history)
identical(replayed, cleaned)
stopifnot(identical(replayed, cleaned))
```

This compares the whole experiment, including its assay, annotations and
pipeline metadata. Exact replay assumes the same original input, package
versions and random-number generator configuration; seeds are recorded in the
step parameters.

## Create a pipeline manually

When you already know the steps you want, define a recipe with
`glyclean_pipeline()`. Omit the experiment argument and use full argument names
for any parameters:

```{r}
recipe <- glyclean_pipeline(
  normalize_total_area(),
  impute_min_prob(q = 0.01, seed = 42)
)
recipe
```

Building the recipe does not preprocess any data. Supply the experiment when
you apply it:

```{r}
from_recipe <- apply_pipeline(original, recipe)
identical(from_recipe, cleaned)
stopifnot(identical(from_recipe, cleaned))
```

Recipes can also include `auto_*()` calls to choose methods when they are
applied. The resulting experiment's history records the concrete operations
that ran, ready to inspect or replay.

## Treat zeros as missing measurements

When zeros in your data represent missing measurements, explicitly convert them
before imputation. `zero_to_na()` changes exact zeros only; it does not change
nonzero values or decide how to impute. It is recorded like any other operation:

```{r}
zero_recipe <- glyclean_pipeline(zero_to_na(), impute_min_prob(seed = 42))
zero_cleaned <- apply_pipeline(original, zero_recipe)
stopifnot(identical(
  apply_pipeline(original, get_pipeline(zero_cleaned)), zero_cleaned
))
```
